trust_decision.summary: The server decides which glob/wildcard characters an identity template expression may substitute into an authorisation-relevant string (ACL policy path, PKI allowed_uri_sans/allowed_domains, SSH allowed_users/allowed_domains); at the pinned commit the substitution is performed verbatim in identitytpl.PopulateString, which all four consumers call with no character filter.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Templated Policies ... via Wildcard Characters', and parsePaths is where a templated policy path key is rendered through identitytpl.PopulateString before being matched against request paths; it is the first function an engineer greps for.

fix_sites.entry_point: any token-authenticated API request that compiles an ACL from a templated policy (vault/policy/policy_store.go:679)
any token-authenticated API request (ACL build); blocked set derived from the policy's allow_*_in_substitutions flags
sys/policy/:name and sys/policies/acl/:name field schema (allow_wildcards_in_substitutions / allow_slashes_in_substitutions)
public SDK API: framework.PopulateIdentityTemplate (wrapper used by PKI and SSH at the pinned commit)
pki/issue/:role and pki/sign/:role (allowed_domains / CN / SAN validation)
ssh/sign/:role and ssh/issue/:role (renderPrincipal for allowed_users and host allowed_domains)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: identitytpl lives in the separate sdk module (sdk/go.mod) as a generic identity-template helper, not in policy or in the PKI/SSH engines; a solver can argue the wildcard policy belongs in vault/policy and leave the shared primitive untouched, which silently leaves builtin/logical/pki and builtin/logical/ssh injecting metadata verbatim.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Wildcards written by the administrator must keep working: a policy definition may legitimately contain globs (path "secret/*") and a PKI role may legitimately set allow_glob_domains with '*' in a static allowed_domains entry; the published fix therefore blocks only characters that arrive through a substitution and only in the rendered value, so an over-broad fix that rejects '*' in the whole rule or in the final rendered domain breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: wildcard arriving via a substituted value versus a wildcard in the template definition itself (the definition must stay allowed)
different forbidden sets per consumer: '/' + '*' + '+' for ACL policy paths, '*' for PKI allowed_uri_sans/allowed_domains, ',' for SSH allowed_users/allowed_domains
substituted value embedded in a larger literal with a static prefix/suffix (spiffe://domain/users/*, *.example.com, svc-{{...}})
the value in the entity metadata of the request token, and in group/alias metadata reached by the other identitytpl handlers
several template expressions in one string (the substitution loop runs per {{...}} piece)
per-policy/per-role opt-out booleans that must default to false on both the create and the patch/merge route

O8_uncovered_routes.route: framework.PopulateIdentityTemplate still renders entity metadata with no blocked characters; the published fix only marks it deprecated in a comment, so any backend still calling the SDK wrapper injects wildcards/commas unfiltered
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is a public SDK helper aimed at out-of-tree backend plugins, and after the fix no in-tree caller remains, so the in-repo authorisation surface is considered covered

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ssh default_extensions templating renders substituted values with no blocked characters even though the same sshRole gained allow_commas_in_substitutions for allowed_users/allowed_domains in the same commit
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: extension values are free-form strings, not comma-separated allow-lists, so the injection the advisory describes cannot apply to them
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fixed ssh site (0 files)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second templated allow-list in the PKI role, e.g. allowed_other_sans_template or allowed_serial_numbers_template, validated with glob.Glob like allowed_uri_sans
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the role already carries four templated allow-lists validated in the same two functions, so a maintainer copying the pattern for another SAN class is a one-file change

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a compatibility shim that keeps calling identitytpl.PopulateString without BlockedSubstitutions, next to the new call sites
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the published fix itself leaves this wrapper in place and only deprecates it, so shipping a second helper that forgets the block is exactly what a maintainer does under API-compatibility pressure

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second ACL-compile path for inline token policies (the additionalPolicies argument) that must derive its blocked set from the token's policy rather than from a stored Policy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ACL() already iterates pre-fetched policies that never came from the policy store, so a maintainer could plausibly route inline policies through a separate compile call

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a host-certificate principal glob check (validateValidPrincipalForHosts) that treats allowed_domains values as patterns while the user-principal path treats them as literals
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: two validators for the same role field already coexist in this file, one per certificate type
